Assertion (A): Arteries have thick and elastic walls.
Reason (R): Blood flows through the arteries under high pressure as it is pumped out of the heart.

Assertion (A): Insulin helps in regulating the level of sugar in the blood.
Reason (R): Insulin is secreted by the thyroid gland.

Assertion (A): Plants raised by vegetative propagation are genetically similar to the parent plant.
Reason (R): Vegetative propagation involves the fusion of male and female gametes.

Assertion (A): The use of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) is being reduced all over the world.
Reason (R): A molecule of ozone is made up of three atoms of oxygen.
Why is the rate of breathing in aquatic organisms much faster than that in terrestrial organisms? Give one reason.
State two differences between the transport of materials in xylem and in phloem.
Name the plant hormone responsible for (a) the elongation of the stem and (b) the wilting of leaves. State one more function of each.
What is the role of the seminal vesicles and the prostate gland in the human male reproductive system?
How did Mendel's experiments with pea plants show that a trait may be dominant or recessive? Explain with one example.
Why are substances like polythene bags called non-biodegradable? State two ways in which they harm the environment.
Describe the digestion of food in the small intestine of human beings. In your answer, state the role of (a) bile juice, (b) pancreatic juice and (c) villi.
How is the movement of the leaves of the 'touch-me-not' plant different from the bending of a shoot towards light? Give three points of difference.

Describe the events that take place in a flower from the time a pollen grain lands on a suitable stigma until the formation of the zygote. What do the ovary and the ovule develop into after fertilisation?

A plant with blue flowers (BB) is crossed with a plant with white flowers (bb).
(a) What will be the colour of the flowers in the F₁ generation? Give a reason.
(b) If the F₁ plants are self-pollinated, what percentage of the F₂ plants will have white flowers?
(c) State the ratio of BB : Bb plants in the F₂ generation.

Farmers around a village pond used a pesticide on their crops for several years. Rain water carried a part of this pesticide into the pond. A study of the pond showed that the concentration of the pesticide was 0.02 ppm in water, 5 ppm in small fish and 25 ppm in the fish-eating birds living near the pond. The pesticide could not be broken down by the organisms and so it kept collecting in their bodies.
(a) Name the phenomenon shown by the rising concentration of the pesticide.
(b) Why do the birds have the highest concentration of the pesticide?
(c) Suggest two practices that farmers can adopt to reduce this problem.
OR
(c) Write a food chain of four trophic levels operating in this pond and name the organisms that form the third trophic level.

The kidneys remove nitrogenous wastes such as urea from the blood. If both kidneys of a person stop working, the wastes build up in the blood and can be fatal. Such a person is treated with an artificial kidney, a process called haemodialysis. The patient's blood is passed through long tubes with a selectively permeable lining, which are dipped in a tank of dialysing fluid. The wastes pass from the blood into this fluid and the purified blood is returned to the patient.
(a) Name the main nitrogenous waste removed by the kidneys in humans.
(b) Why should the dialysing fluid have the same concentration of salts and glucose as normal blood?
(c) State two differences between the working of a natural kidney and that of an artificial kidney.
OR
(c) Explain how the amount of water reabsorbed in the nephron changes on a hot day when a person has drunk very little water.

(a) Name the parts of the human female reproductive system where (i) eggs are produced, (ii) fertilisation takes place and (iii) the embryo is implanted.
(b) How does the embryo get its nourishment inside the mother's body?
(c) What happens when the egg is not fertilised?
OR
(a) What is contraception? List three different methods of contraception and state how each one works.
(b) Why is the use of a condom also considered important for health reasons?

(a) What is meant by double circulation of blood? Why is it necessary in human beings?
(b) Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle?
(c) State two differences between arteries and veins.
OR
(a) List the three events that occur during photosynthesis.
(b) How do desert plants take up carbon dioxide and still prevent the loss of water?
(c) Describe an activity to show that sunlight is necessary for photosynthesis.

Assertion (A): White silver chloride turns grey when it is kept in sunlight.
Reason (R): Silver chloride decomposes into silver and chlorine in the presence of sunlight.

Reason (R): Hydrogen chloride produces hydrogen ions only in the presence of water.

Reason (R): Gold and platinum are highly reactive metals.

Assertion (A): Soaps do not form lather easily with hard water.
Reason (R): Hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts, which react with soap to form an insoluble scum.

(a) Why does he shift the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline?

(b) Metals are used for making school bells.

Write balanced chemical equations for the following reactions and name the type of each reaction:
(a) Barium chloride solution is mixed with sodium sulphate solution.
(b) Zinc granules are added to dilute sulphuric acid.
(c) Ferrous sulphate crystals are heated strongly.

(a) What is the chlor-alkali process? Write the chemical equation of the reaction involved.
(b) Name the gas produced at the anode and the gas produced at the cathode in this process.
(c) State one use of each of these two gases.

A metal M occurs in nature as its carbonate ore, MCO₃. The metal lies in the middle of the reactivity series.
(a) Name the two main steps used to obtain the metal from this ore.
(b) Write the chemical equations for these steps, taking zinc as the metal.
(c) Name the process used to refine the impure metal so obtained.

(a) Distinguish between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons on the basis of the flame they produce on burning.
(b) What is hydrogenation? Write a chemical equation to show it.
(c) State one industrial application of hydrogenation.

Three clean iron nails were kept in three test tubes for a week. Test tube P had tap water, so the nail was in contact with both air and water. Test tube Q had boiled distilled water covered with a layer of oil. Test tube R had dry air with some anhydrous calcium chloride. After a week, only the nail in test tube P had rusted. Rusting damages bridges, ships and car bodies, and a lot of money is spent every year to prevent it.
(a) What does this experiment tell us about the conditions necessary for rusting?
(b) Why was a layer of oil added in test tube Q?
(c) What is galvanisation? Why does a galvanised iron article not rust even when the zinc coating is scratched?
OR
(c) What is an alloy? Name the metals mixed with iron to make stainless steel and state how this helps.

Most dirt is oily in nature and oil does not dissolve in water. A soap molecule has two ends: a long hydrocarbon chain and an ionic end. When soap is added to water containing oily dirt, the soap molecules arrange themselves in clusters around the oil droplets. Rinsing then removes the dirt. In hard water, however, soap forms a sticky white solid and a lot of soap is wasted. Detergents were developed to overcome this problem.
(a) What name is given to the cluster of soap molecules formed around an oil droplet?
(b) Which end of the soap molecule attaches to the oil droplet and which end faces the water?
(c) Why does soap form a sticky solid (scum) with hard water? Why do detergents not form it?
OR
(c) Would a micelle be formed if soap were dissolved in ethanol instead of water? Give a reason for your answer.

(b) What is observed when ethanoic acid is added to sodium hydrogencarbonate? Write the equation.
(c) Why is pure ethanoic acid called glacial acetic acid?
(d) State one chemical test to distinguish ethanol from ethanoic acid.
OR
(a) What is a homologous series? State three characteristics of a homologous series.
(b) Draw the structures of the two isomers of butane (C₄H₁₀).
(c) Why does carbon form compounds mainly by covalent bonding?

(c) What is meant by water of crystallisation? Give one example of a salt that has it.

(b) State two uses of washing soda.

In a house, all the appliances are connected in parallel across the live and neutral wires, and each appliance has its own switch. The supply reaches the house at 220 V. The wiring has two separate circuits, one of 5 A rating for bulbs and fans and another of 15 A rating for appliances such as geysers and air coolers. A third wire, the earth wire, is connected to the metal body of appliances such as the electric iron and the refrigerator.
(a) Why are household appliances connected in parallel and not in series? Give one reason.
(b) What is the function of the earth wire?
(c) What is overloading? State two ways in which it can be caused.
OR
(c) A geyser of 2 kW and an electric kettle of 1.5 kW are switched on together in the 15 A circuit at 220 V. Find the total current drawn and state whether the fuse will blow.

An eye specialist tests the eyesight of two patients. For the first patient, Asha, the prescription for the lens is +2.0 D. For the second patient, Imran, the prescription is −0.5 D. The power of a lens tells us how strongly it converges or diverges light, and opticians often place lenses in contact to get the required power.
(a) What type of lens is prescribed for Asha?
(b) Calculate the focal length of the lens prescribed for Imran.
(c) Define one dioptre. If lenses of power +2.0 D and −0.5 D are placed in contact, find the power and the focal length of the combination.
OR
(c) Draw a ray diagram to show how a convex lens corrects the defect of vision in which nearby objects cannot be seen clearly.

(a) State Ohm's law. Describe the shape of the V-I graph for a metallic conductor.
(b) List the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends.
(c) A 4 Ω resistor is connected in series with a parallel combination of a 6 Ω resistor and a 3 Ω resistor. The arrangement is connected to a 6 V battery. Find (i) the total resistance of the circuit, (ii) the current drawn from the battery and (iii) the current through the 6 Ω resistor.
OR
(a) What is the heating effect of electric current? Write the expression for the heat produced in a resistor.
(b) Why is tungsten used for the filament of an electric bulb?
(c) A 100 W bulb and a 60 W bulb are connected in parallel to a 220 V supply. Find the total current drawn from the supply.

(a) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formed by a convex lens when the object is placed between F₁ and 2F₁. State the nature of the image.
(b) Write the lens formula and state the sign convention used for the object distance.
(c) An object is placed 30 cm from a concave lens of focal length 15 cm. Find the position and the magnification of the image.
OR
(a) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed between the pole and the principal focus. State the nature of the image.
(b) Define the radius of curvature of a spherical mirror and write its relation with the focal length.
(c) An object is placed 10 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position and nature of the image.
